A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSR method and investigation of high-dimensional Bayesian optimization. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original GP simulations, optimization experiments on four real-world benchmarks, and appendix analyses of synthetic functions and benchmark structure.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds SVM/Rover evaluations, comparator results, and acquisition-optimizer diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains MSR's MLE fitting, sqrt(d)/10 length-scale initialization, ARD Matern-5/2 kernel, LogEI, and RAASP sampling. The new implementation appendix documents these components without establishing a changed proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The actual optimization evaluation expands from four to six application benchmarks by adding SVM (388 dimensions) and Rover (60 dimensions), with results in Figures 8-10 and 13. SVM's earlier mention in v1 was not an optimization evaluation. The original application and synthetic-function coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds TuRBO (RAASP) and MLE with fixed ln(2) initialization plus RAASP, introducing both a trust-region comparator and a control separating initialization from local sampling. TuRBO's presence in v1's synthetic-function appendix does not constitute participation in its earlier real-world comparison.

E3.justification: The new RAASP comparison evaluates acquisition-optimizer effort through gradient-update counts (v2 Figure 12), adding a diagnostic metric and evaluation procedure. Existing benchmark budgets remain unchanged; the optimizer settings newly specified in Appendix B are disclosures, not demonstrated revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds the fixed-initialization-plus-RAASP control in Figures 8-9 and an analysis of acquisition-optimizer convergence effort in Figure 12. These extend the existing initialization/locality investigations; the synthetic-function comparisons, difficult GP example, and benchmark-structure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing repetition counts, standard-error reporting, and two-sided Wilcoxon testing remain unchanged. The additional result curves and gradient-update histograms do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds SVM/Rover performance and diagnostic results, TuRBO and fixed-initialization-plus-RAASP comparison curves, and Figure 12's finding that RAASP reduces acquisition-optimizer gradient updates. The numerical ranking and benchmark-structure tables from v1 Tables 1-3 are retained as v2 Tables 2-4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and reasoning in Section 3 and Appendix A are retained. Adding the missing theta_i reference before Equation 10 clarifies notation without changing the derivative or introducing a new derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that vanishing gradients and locality explain important HDBO behavior, that MLE/MSR achieves competitive performance without length-scale hyperpriors, and that RAASP stabilizes length-scale estimates. The additional experiments and revised wording do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion explicitly identifies the GP-surrogate scope and leaves extension to random forests and Bayesian neural networks for future work. It also proposes combining MSR with trust regions, embeddings, and additive structures. Appendix B.2 connects early acquisition-optimizer convergence to maxima near good observations.

D1.justification: New Appendix B specifies RAASP's perturbation standard deviation of 10^-3, the 2:1:1 mixture of global and two local candidate types, Boltzmann selection, and L-BFGS-B optimization capped at 2000 iterations. These fill implementation gaps without establishing that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hoang et al. (2018) and Bardou et al. (2024) to the discussion of additive approaches. A Section 2 footnote identifies the Xu and Zhe preprint being discussed and acknowledges their later concurrent development of a similar initialization strategy, refining the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include light wording and acronym edits, additional future-work paragraphs, an implementation appendix, and consequent relabeling of the earlier appendices B/C as C/D.

P2.justification: The central empirical displays expand substantially: Figures 8-10 and the former Figure 12 gain two benchmark panels, comparison legends and colors change, and v2 adds method-summary Table 1 and gradient-update Figure 12. Existing appendix figures and tables are also redistributed while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: The added benchmarks, TuRBO comparison, complementary RAASP control, and implementation details improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility of an already substantial study. Integration remains imperfect: Section 4 still refers to four applications, and some color references no longer match the revised legends. The useful evidence and documentation additions outweigh these limited presentation problems.
